tools.name: accept_dataset_agreement
tools.description: Accept the Dataset License Agreement for a quoted order on the buyer's behalf. Call ONLY after the buyer explicitly approves the tier, clip count, price, and the full agreement text. Paid tiers move to awaiting_payment; the free evaluation sample goes straight to Stockfilm's manual review.

agreement_sha256.description: sha256 of the agreement text the buyer reviewed (from get_dataset_agreement or describe_training_dataset). Proves the current version was shown.

confirmed.description: Set true only after the user explicitly approves the tier, clip count, price, and the full agreement text.

legal_name.description: Legal name of the licensee organization

order_token.description: Private order_token returned by quote_training_dataset. Keep it private.

signer_name.description: Name of the person authorizing the purchase on the licensee's behalf

tools.name: build_rough_cut
tools.description: Auto-assemble a timed sequence of vintage clips into a video timeline based on a description. Returns an ordered list of clips with durations. Great for creating edit lists or storyboards.

query.description: Natural language description of the video sequence (e.g. 'american road trip summer vacation 1960s')

target_seconds.description: Target timeline length in seconds (20-600, default 60)

tools.name: check_clip_rights
tools.description: Verify a clip is eligible for a given intended use (commercial, editorial, broadcast, etc.) before licensing.

intended_use.description: Intended use: commercial, editorial, documentary, internal_corporate, broadcast, digital, or ai_training. AI training requires a separate written agreement.

tools.name: create_4k_checkout
tools.description: Create or resume Stripe hosted checkout for a quoted 4K license. Call ONLY after the user explicitly approves the quoted clip, total price, resolution, license scope, territory, term, and terms. Returns a checkout URL and private order token. The user pays securely in Stripe; never collect card details in chat. Repeating the same quote reuses its order. Creating checkout is not proof of purchase.

confirmed.description: Set true only after the user explicitly approves the quoted clip, resolution, price, scope, territory, term, and terms link.

quote_token.description: Private quote_token returned by quote_4k_license. Never expose it in public links or logs.

tools.name: create_dataset_checkout
tools.description: Start payment for an accepted dataset order. Card orders (proxy media, up to $10,000) return a Stripe checkout_url the buyer pays in a browser; never collect card details in chat. 4K, research, and larger orders return a bank-wire invoice (number, amount, due date, reference) that is also emailed to the buyer; the buyer's finance team pays it. Repeating the call reuses the open checkout or invoice. Payment is not delivery: every order is reviewed by a person at Stockfilm after the funds clear.

tools.name: describe_training_dataset
tools.description: Describe Stockfilm's AI-training dataset product: eligible catalog counts, the three fixed-price tiers (free evaluation sample; $25,000 research for academic institutions; commercial at $3.00/clip proxies or $10.00/clip 4K masters, $10,000 minimum), payment rails (card for small proxy orders, bank wire for 4K and larger orders), available filters, the agreement version and sha256, and the purchase workflow. AI-training rights are sold only this way, never per clip and never exclusively.

tools.name: find_similar_footage
tools.description: Find visually similar vintage clips by providing a clip ID. Returns clips with similar visual content from the Stockfilm archive.

clip_id.description: Clip ID to find similar footage for

tools.name: get_4k_order
tools.description: Verify a 4K order's payment with Stripe and retrieve the license, receipt, and private master download after payment. Requires the private order token from create_4k_checkout. May activate an already-paid license. Never claim purchase completed until purchase_completed is true. If delivery_status is preparing, retry later. Poll no faster than once every 10 seconds. Keep the token and download URL private.

order_token.description: Private order_token returned by create_4k_checkout. Keep this token and returned download URLs private.

tools.name: get_clip_details
tools.description: Get full details for a specific Stockfilm clip including description, year shot, location, price, resolution, thumbnail URL, and preview URL.

clip_id.description: The clip ID from search results

tools.name: get_dataset_agreement
tools.description: Fetch the full text of the Stockfilm Dataset License Agreement with its version and sha256. Show the text to the buyer before accept_dataset_agreement; the sha256 must be sent back on acceptance.

tools.name: get_dataset_order
tools.description: Check a dataset order: payment state, Stockfilm's approval decision, and, once delivered, download.manifest_url for the metadata files, signed license, and per-clip media URLs. Poll no more than every 10 minutes while awaiting approval. Never report delivery until status is delivered.

tools.name: license_clip
tools.description: Get licensing options for a clip without charging the user. The website offers 4K masters for eligible clips; the separate x402 product is 144p. Review availability, exact price, and terms on the clip page before purchase. This tool does not issue a license or process payment.

tools.name: quote_4k_license
tools.description: Quote an eligible, unwatermarked 4K master using the website's direct license pricing. Verifies actual resolution and licensing availability. Ask for the buyer email and desired use, territory, and term. Does not charge the user. Show the complete quote and terms before requesting checkout approval. AI training is excluded.

customer_email.description: Buyer email for the license and receipt; ask the user, never invent one.

territory.description: User-selected territory: worldwide, north_america, europe, asia_pacific, or single_country.

usage_scope.description: User-selected use: commercial, editorial, internal_corporate, broadcast_tv, or social_web. AI training is excluded.

tools.name: quote_training_dataset
tools.description: Create a fixed-price dataset quote for a filtered subset and get a private order_token. Freezes the exact clip list. Ask the buyer for their email, organization, and intended use first. Does not charge anyone. Show the buyer the tier, clip count, hours, price, payment method (card or bank wire), and the agreement before asking them to accept.

countries.description: Country names as they appear in the catalog, e.g. ["United States", "France"]

decades.description: Decades to include, e.g. ["1950s", "1960s"]. Default: all six, 1930s–1980s.

exclude_logos.description: Exclude clips with logos or trademarks (implies reviewed_only)

exclude_minors.description: Exclude clips where minors are visible (implies reviewed_only)

exclude_music.description: Exclude clips with audible music (implies reviewed_only)

exclude_people.description: Exclude clips where people are visible (implies reviewed_only)

max_clips.description: Cap the selection at this many clips (stable pseudo-random sample of the matches)

max_risk.description: Highest clearance risk to include: low, medium, or high (default)

query.description: Free text matched against titles, descriptions, and keywords

require_4k_master.description: Only clips with a restored 4K master online (forced on for 4k media)

reviewed_only.description: Only clips with clearance flags populated. Default true.

customer_email.description: Buyer's work email at their organization's own domain, used for the order, invoice, and delivery; ask the user, never invent one. Consumer and disposable mailboxes (Gmail, Outlook, iCloud, Proton, etc.) are refused.

intended_use.description: What the buyer intends to train or evaluate with the data (10–2000 characters). Shown to the person who approves the order.

tools.name: scope_training_dataset
tools.description: Count how many clips and hours match a filter set for a dataset tier, with the fixed price. Free, reserves nothing, needs no buyer details. Use it to iterate on filters before quoting.

countries.description: Country names as they appear in the catalog, e.g. ["United States", "France"]

decades.description: Decades to include, e.g. ["1950s", "1960s"]. Default: all six, 1930s–1980s.

exclude_logos.description: Exclude clips with logos or trademarks (implies reviewed_only)

exclude_minors.description: Exclude clips where minors are visible (implies reviewed_only)

exclude_music.description: Exclude clips with audible music (implies reviewed_only)

exclude_people.description: Exclude clips where people are visible (implies reviewed_only)

max_clips.description: Cap the selection at this many clips (stable pseudo-random sample of the matches)

max_risk.description: Highest clearance risk to include: low, medium, or high (default)

query.description: Free text matched against titles, descriptions, and keywords

require_4k_master.description: Only clips with a restored 4K master online (forced on for 4k media)

reviewed_only.description: Only clips with clearance flags populated. Default true.

media_resolution.description: proxy (watermarked 256x144 analysis MP4s, default) or 4k (restored masters, commercial tier only, always paid by bank wire; limits the set to clips with a master online)

tier.description: evaluation (free, ≤100 clips, proxies), research ($25,000 flat, ≤25,000 clips, proxies, accredited academic institutions only), or commercial ($3.00/clip proxies or $10.00/clip 4K masters, $10,000 minimum, ≤50,000 clips). Default commercial.

tools.name: search_vintage_footage
tools.description: Search Stockfilm's archive of authentic vintage home movie clips from the 1930s-1980s. Returns clips with metadata, pricing, thumbnails, and licensing info. All footage is real 8mm/Super 8 film — no AI-generated content.

limit.description: Number of results to return (1-50, default 10)

query.description: Natural language search query. Be descriptive: '1960s california family barbecue' works better than just 'family'.
